rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation of the heavens and earth without fatigue proves God can resurrect the dead; He created them by command, and they obeyed without resistance.
rows.anchor: بلا ممانعة ولا مخالفة، بل طائعة مجيبة خائفة وجلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the Fire, the disbelievers can only acknowledge that its reality is true, then are told to taste punishment for their disbelief.
rows.anchor: أي: لا يسعهم إلا الاعتراف، {قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet must endure his people’s denial as the resolute messengers endured the denial of their peoples.
rows.anchor: أي: على تكذيب قومهم لهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best-known enumeration of the resolute messengers is Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad, whom God names in al-Ahzab and al-Shura.
rows.anchor: وأشهرها أنهم: نوح، وإبراهيم، وموسى، وعيسى، وخاتم الأنبياء كلهم محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possible reading takes all messengers as resolute, with min explaining the class rather than selecting some members; God knows best.
rows.anchor: وقد يحتمل أن يكون المراد بأولي العزم جميع الرسل، وتكون {من} في قوله: {من الرسل} لبيان الجنس

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: She reports that the Prophet endured successive fasting days and said God required from him the same patience required of the resolute messengers, over hardship and what they loved.
rows.anchor: ظل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم صائما ثم طواه، ثم ظل صائما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told not to hasten the punishment of his opponents, as in commands to leave deniers respite.
rows.anchor: أي: لا تستعجل لهم حلول العقوبة بهم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On seeing the promised Judgment, people will regard their residence in the world and the intermediate realm as only an hour, given the ordeal and length of that Day.
rows.anchor: استقصروا مدة لبثهم في الدنيا وفي البرزخ حين عاينوا يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir offers two readings of “a proclamation”: it may describe their stay as sufficient, or identify the Qur’an itself as the proclamation.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جرير: يحتمل معنيين، أحدهما: أن يكون تقديره:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God destroys only those who deserve destruction and punishment; this is an expression of His justice.
rows.anchor: وهذا من عدله تعالى أنه لا يعذب إلا من يستحق العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should patiently bear what the deniers say and withdraw from them graciously.
rows.anchor: يعني: المكذبين، اصبر عليهم واهجرهم هجرا جميلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before the Night Journey, the obligatory prayers were two: dawn before sunrise and afternoon before sunset; night vigil was obligatory on the Prophet and community for a year, then abrogated for the community.
rows.anchor: وكانت الصلاة المفروضة قبل الإسراء ثنتين قبل طلوع الشمس في وقت الفجر، وقبل الغروب في وقت العصر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Night Journey established five prayers, including dawn and afternoon at the times named here.
rows.anchor: ثم بعد ذلك نسخ الله ذلك كله ليلة الإسراء بخمس صلوات، ولكن منهن

rows.speaker: جرير بن عبد الله
rows.claim: The Prophet likened believers’ future sight of their Lord to seeing the full moon without obstruction and urged them to preserve the prayers before sunrise and sunset; the report is in the canonical collections.
rows.anchor: عن جرير بن عبد الله قال: كنا جلوسا عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فنظر إلى القمر ليلة البدر

rows.speaker: الترمذي
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi transmits an extra version through Abu Hisham al-Rifa‘i; Ibn Kathir says it is unfamiliar and known only by this route.
rows.anchor: ورواه الترمذي عن أبي هشام الرفاعي، عن محمد بن فضيل، به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added material attached to Ibn Abbas’s report is unfamiliar and comes only through this route; Rashidin ibn Kurayb is weak, and the addition may be Ibn Abbas’s own stopped statement.
rows.anchor: لا تعرف إلا من هذا الوجه، ورشدين بن كريب ضعيف،

rows.speaker: زيد بن خالد الجهني
rows.claim: After rain at Hudaybiyya, the Prophet said that attributing rain to God’s grace is belief in God and disbelief in stars, while crediting a star is disbelief in God; the report is in the two Sahihs and other collections.
rows.anchor: عن زيد بن خالد الجهني أنه قال: صلى بنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم صلاة الصبح بالحديبية

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says people often meet a rain blessing by disbelief, claiming that a particular star brought it; Muslim alone transmits this route.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: "ما أنزل الله من السماء من بركة

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Another report says people receive divine favor then credit rain to a star; Umar asked al-Abbas when the Pleiades would appear, and rain came on the seventh night after its setting.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إن الله ليصبح القوم بالنعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asking about the customary time rain falls is permissible; the condemned belief is that a star itself causes rain. Ibn Kathir links the issue to another verse on divine mercy.
rows.anchor: وهذا محمول على السؤال عن الوقت الذي أجرى الله فيه العادة بإنزال المطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For worldly people, worldly life amounts to play, distraction, adornment, mutual boasting, and competition in wealth and children, as another verse describes desire for worldly goods.
rows.anchor: إنما حاصل أمرها عند أهلها هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transient life is compared to rain that comes after people have despaired of it.
rows.anchor: وهو: المطر الذي يأتي بعد قنوط الناس، كما قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The crop delights its cultivators, just as worldly life delights disbelievers, who are especially attached to it; the green crop yellows and breaks into dry fragments.
rows.anchor: أي: يعجب الزراع نبات ذلك الزرع الذي نبت بالغيث؛

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The crop’s decline illustrates both worldly life and human aging, from fresh youth through weakening maturity to frail old age.
rows.anchor: هكذا الحياة الدنيا تكون أولا شابة، ثم تكتهل، ثم تكون عجوزا شوهاء،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hereafter brings either severe punishment or forgiveness and God’s good pleasure; the present life is only a deceptive enjoyment.
rows.anchor: إما عذاب شديد، وإما مغفرة من الله ورضوان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly life is a brief, deceptive provision for one who relies on it and imagines there is no other abode or resurrection; compared with the Hereafter it is insignificant.
rows.anchor: فإنه يغتر بها وتعجبه حتى يعتقد أنه لا دار سواها ولا معاد وراءها،

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report says a whip’s-width place in Paradise is better than the world and all it contains; Ibn Kathir notes that the report is authentic without the added wording quoted here.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "موضع سوط في الجنة خير

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: The Prophet said Paradise is nearer to each person than a sandal strap, and so is the Fire; al-Bukhari alone gives this route.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "للجنة أقرب إلى أحدكم من شراك نعله،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because both good and evil are near, people should hurry to obedience and avoid forbidden acts that erase sins and earn reward.
rows.anchor: ففي هذا الحديث دليل على اقتراب الخير والشر من الإنسان،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised garden’s width is the breadth of the kind of heavens and earth, as in another verse.
rows.anchor: والمراد جنس السماء والأرض

rows.speaker: الفقراء المهاجرون
rows.claim: Poor emigrants lamented that wealthy companions matched their prayer and fasting but could also give charity and free slaves; the Prophet taught post-prayer glorification, takbir, and praise, then said this was God’s bounty.
rows.anchor: أن فقراء المهاجرين قالوا: يا رسول الله، ذهب أهل الدثور بالدرجات العلى

rows.speaker: أبيه
rows.claim: When impoverished barefoot people arrived, the Prophet urged charity, even half a date; an Ansari brought a large bundle and others followed. He said the initiator of a good or bad practice bears its reward or burden and that of later imitators; Muslim alone transmits this route.
rows.anchor: عن المنذر ابن جرير، عن أبيه قال: كنا عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في صدر النهار، قال: فجاءه قوم حفاة عراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to fear God includes doing what He commands and leaving what He forbids.
rows.anchor: أمر بتقواه، وهي تشمل فعل ما به أمر، وترك ما عنه زجر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should take account of themselves before being judged and prepare righteous deeds for the Resurrection and presentation before God.
rows.anchor: أي: حاسبوا أنفسكم قبل أن تحاسبوا، وانظروا ماذا ادخرتم لأنفسكم من الأعمال الصالحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated command to fear God reinforces the warning that God knows every act and state, large or small.
rows.anchor: تأكيد ثان، {إن الله خبير بما تعملون} أي: اعلموا أنه عالم بجميع أعمالكم وأحوالكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgetting God makes people neglect their own afterlife interests; such people leave obedience and lose on the Day of Return, as in the warning not to let wealth and children distract from remembrance.
rows.anchor: لا تنسوا ذكر الله فينسيكم العمل لمصالح أنفسكم

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
rows.claim: In a sermon, Abu Bakr urged people to finish their appointed lives in God’s service, remember past rulers who now lie beneath rocks, and use scripture as light; he cited the praise of Zechariah’s household for hastening to good works.
rows.anchor: في خطبة أبي بكر الصديق، رضي الله عنه: أما تعلمون أنكم تغدون وتروحون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers are urged to remember God abundantly and not let wealth or children distract them; whoever is absorbed by worldly adornment instead of obedience loses himself and his family at Resurrection.
rows.anchor: آمرا لعباده المؤمنين بكثرة ذكره وناهيا لهم عن أن تشغلهم الأموال والأولاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They should spend in obedience before death, since every negligent person regrets at death and asks for even a brief reprieve to make up what was missed, too late.
rows.anchor: فكل مفرط يندم عند الاحتضار، ويسأل طول المدة ولو شيئا يسيرا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once a person’s appointed term arrives, God gives no extension; He knows who would sincerely reform and who would return to worse conduct if sent back.
rows.anchor: أي: لا ينظر أحدا بعد حلول أجله، وهو أعلم وأخبر بمن يكون صادقا في قوله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says someone with means for Hajj or liable zakat who neglects it will ask to return at death; he gives two hundred as the zakat threshold and provisions plus a mount for Hajj.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: من كان له مال يبلغه حج بيت ربه، أو تجب عليه فيه زكاة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says Sufyan ibn Uyayna and others transmit Ibn Abbas’s statement in stopped form, which is sounder, and he weakens Abu Janab; al-Dahhak’s report from Ibn Abbas is disconnected.
rows.anchor: وهو أصح، وضعف أبا جناب الكلبي. قلت: رواية الضحاك عن ابن عباس فيها انقطاع،

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: The Prophet said God does not delay a soul after its term; an apparent increase in lifespan comes when God grants a person righteous children whose prayers reach him in the grave.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء، رضي الله عنه، قال: ذكرنا عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الزيادة في العمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Gathering is Resurrection, when the first and last generations assemble on one plain, hear the caller, and are all visible, as other verses say.
rows.anchor: وهو يوم القيامة، سمي بذلك لأنه يجمع فيه الأولون والآخرون في صعيد واحد،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas calls the Day of Mutual Loss one of Resurrection’s names and explains that Paradise’s people gain against Hell’s people; Qatada and Mujahid agree.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هو اسم من أسماء يوم القيامة. وذلك أن أهل الجنة يغبنون أهل النار.

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: There is no greater loss than some people entering Paradise while others are consigned to Hell.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل بن حيان: لا غبن أعظم من أن يدخل هؤلاء إلى الجنة،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and many early and later scholars understand the housing rule to mean the husband’s capacity.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وغير واحد: يعني سعتكم.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says that if a man has no separate residence, he should house her beside his own house.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: إن لم تجد إلا جنب بيتك فأسكنها فيه.

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: Mujahid says the prohibition on constraining a divorced woman forbids pressuring her to pay money for release or forcing her from her residence.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل بن حيان: يعني يضاجرها لتفتدي منه بمالها أو تخرج من مسكنه.

rows.speaker: أبو الضحى
rows.claim: Abu al-Duha says a husband might divorce his wife, then take her back when only two days of the waiting period remain, thereby constraining her.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الضحى: {ولا تضاروهن لتضيقوا عليهن} قال: يطلقها، فإذا بقي يومان راجعها.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Many scholars say support for a pregnant divorced woman applies to an irrevocable divorce, since a revocably divorced wife is owed support whether pregnant or not.
rows.anchor: قال كثير من العلماء منهم ابن عباس، وطائفة من السلف، وجماعات من الخلف: هذه في البائن،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others say the passage concerns revocable divorces; pregnancy is singled out because it usually lasts beyond the waiting period, so support to birth must be explicit.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل السياق كله في الرجعيات، وإنما نص على الإنفاق على الحامل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jurists disagree whether support is owed to the woman herself by virtue of her status or only for the fetus; al-Shafi‘i and others record both positions.
rows.anchor: واختلف العلماء: هل النفقة لها بواسطة الحمل، أم للحمل وحده؟ على قولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After childbirth ends the waiting period, a divorced mother may nurse or refuse; she should first give the essential first milk, and if she nurses she earns the customary wage or an agreed fee.
rows.anchor: ولها حينئذ أن ترضع الولد، ولها أن تمتنع منه، ولكن بعد أن تغذيه باللبأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parents should deal fairly without harming each other; if they cannot agree on nursing fees, the father may hire another nurse, though the mother has priority if she accepts the same wage.
rows.anchor: أي: ولتكن أموركم فيما بينكم بالمعروف، من غير إضرار ولا مضارة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A child’s father or guardian should spend according to his means; God does not burden a person beyond what He gives, as another verse says.
rows.anchor: أي: لينفق على المولود والده، أو وليه، بحسب قدرته،

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar tested how Abu Ubayda would use a thousand dinars; seeing that he then wore better clothes and ate better food, Umar said Abu Ubayda had rightly applied this verse.
rows.anchor: سأل عمر بن الخطاب عن أبي عبيدة، فقيل: إنه يلبس الغليظ من الثياب،

rows.speaker: أبو مالك الأشعري
rows.claim: A Prophetic report compares three people giving one tenth of their very different wealth and says their rewards are equal; Ibn Kathir calls this route unusual.
rows.anchor: عن أبي مالك الأشعري -واسمه الحارث-قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ثلاثة نفر، كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God promises relief after hardship and does not break His promise, as the two verses in al-Sharh repeat.
rows.anchor: وعد منه تعالى، ووعده حق، لا يخلفه،

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: In a report, a destitute wife reassures her hungry returning husband that provision is coming; her oven fills with goat meat and the mill turns. The Prophet said the mill would have continued had she left it alone.
rows.anchor: قال أبو هريرة: بينما رجل وامرأة له في السلف الخالي لا يقدران على شيء،

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A second report tells of a poor couple whose mill and cooking vessel fill after the wife prays; the Prophet says the untouched mill would have kept turning until Resurrection.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: دخل رجل على أهله، فلما رأى ما بهم من الحاجة خرج إلى البرية،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden owners are an example for Quraysh: God gave them the great mercy of Muhammad’s mission and abundant blessings, but they answered with denial, rejection, and opposition.
rows.anchor: هذا مثل ضربه الله تعالى لكفار قريش فيما أهدى إليهم من الرحمة العظيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heirs swore to harvest at dawn so that no poor person or petitioner would learn of the crop and receive charity; they made no exception in their oath.
rows.anchor: حلفوا فيما بينهم ليجذن ثمرها ليلا لئلا يعلم بهم فقير ولا سائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A heavenly calamity struck while they slept and left the orchard like a black night, according to Ibn Abbas, or like dry harvested stubble, according to al-Thawri and al-Suddi.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أي كالليل الأسود. وقال الثوري، والسدي: مثل الزرع إذا حصد،

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: A Prophetic report warns that a sin can deprive a person of provision already prepared for him, and applies the warning to the garden owners’ lost crop.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إياكم والمعاصي، إن العبد ليذنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At daybreak they called one another to go harvest if they intended to reap the crop.
rows.anchor: أي: لما كان وقت الصبح نادى بعضهم بعضا ليذهبوا إلى الجذاذ،

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says their crop was grapes.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: كان حرثهم عنبا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They spoke secretly so no one could hear their plan to prevent a poor person from entering the garden that day.
rows.anchor: أي: يتناجون فيما بينهم بحيث لا يسمعون أحدا كلامهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “on resolve” can mean strength and severity; other reported meanings are earnestness, anger, hostility toward the poor, or the name of their town, with the last rejected as far-fetched.
rows.anchor: قال الله تعالى: {وغدوا على حرد} أي: قوة وشدة. وقال مجاهد:

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains “on resolve” as earnestness.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: {وغدوا على حرد} أي: جد

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima explains “on resolve” as anger.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: غيظ.

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Sha‘bi explains the phrase as resolve against the poor.
rows.anchor: وقال الشعبي: {على حرد} على المساكين.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says Harad was the name of their village, but Ibn Kathir dismisses this as a distant interpretation.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: {على حرد} أي: كان اسم قريتهم حرد. فأبعد السدي في قوله هذا!

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They thought they had power over their orchard and could carry out their plan.
rows.anchor: {قادرين} أي: عليها فيما يزعمون ويرومون.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and others say the brothers first thought they had lost their way, then recognized the orchard and realized they had been deprived of its produce.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن عباس وغيره. ثم رجعوا عما كانوا فيه، وتيقنوا أنها هي فقالوا: {بل نحن محرومون}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, Ikrima, Muhammad ibn Ka‘b, al-Rabi‘, al-Dahhak, and Qatada explain their “middle” brother as the fairest and best of them.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وسعيد بن جبير، وعكرمة، ومحمد بن كعب، والربيع بن أنس

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid, al-Suddi, and Ibn Jurayj read “why do you not glorify?” as “why did you not make an exception,” by saying “if God wills.”
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد، والسدي، وابن جريج: {لولا تسبحون} أي: لولا تستثنون.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says that in their time making an exception was expressed as glorification.
rows.anchor: قال السدي: وكان استثناؤهم في ذلك الزمان تسبيحا.

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj identifies the exception formula as saying “if God wills.”
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: هو قول القائل: إن شاء الله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that the middle brother urged them to praise and thank God for what He had given them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه: {قال أوسطهم ألم أقل لكم لولا تسبحون} أي: هلا تسبحون الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They praise God and confess their injustice too late; they blame one another for withholding the poor’s share, admit transgression, and hope God replaces the garden, perhaps in this life or as a reward in the next.
rows.anchor: أتوا بالطاعة حيث لا تنفع، وندموا واعترفوا حيث لا ينجع؛

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Some early scholars say the brothers lived in Yemen near Sana’a or in Abyssinia; their righteous father maintained the garden, kept a year’s provisions, and gave the surplus to the poor, but his sons called this foolish and were punished by losing crop, profit, and charity.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: كانوا من قرية يقال لها ضروان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans are innately impatient: when harmed they panic, are overwhelmed by fear, and despair of future good.
rows.anchor: إذا أصابه الضر فزع وجزع وانخلع قلبه من شدة الرعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When blessed, a person tends to hoard and withhold God’s due from the blessing.
rows.anchor: نعمة من الله بخل بها على غيره، ومنع حق الله فيها.

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet called anxious greed and paralyzing cowardice the worst traits in a man; Abu Dawud gives the same report through this route.
rows.anchor: سمعت أبا هريرة يقول: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "شر ما في رجل شح هالع، وجبن خالع".

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is those God protects and guides: worshippers who maintain their prayers.
rows.anchor: أي: الإنسان من حيث هو متصف بصفات الذم إلا من عصمه الله ووفقه،

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas‘ud, Masruq, and Ibrahim al-Nakha‘i say regular prayer means preserving its times and obligations.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن مسعود، ومسروق، وإبراهيم النخعي.

rows.speaker: عتبة بن عامر
rows.claim: ‘Utba ibn Amir interprets constancy in prayer as stillness and humility, like still, settled water, paralleling another verse.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المراد بالدوام هاهنا السكون والخشوع، كقوله:

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet said the most beloved deeds to God are those done regularly, however few, and that he himself maintained any deed he began.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: "أحب الأعمال إلى الله أدومها وإن قل".

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada relays that Daniel described Muhammad’s community as a people whose prayers would have saved Noah’s, ‘Ad’s, or Thamud’s people from their destruction.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة في قوله: {الذين هم على صلاتهم دائمون} ذكر لنا أن دانيال، عليه السلام،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is only a human recipient of revelation and servant of God; he controls neither people’s guidance nor their misguidance, since all authority belongs to God.
rows.anchor: أي: إنما أنا بشر مثلكم يوحى إلي، وعبد من عباد الله ليس إلي من الأمر شيء

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid, Qatada, and al-Suddi explain “no refuge” as no place of shelter; Qatada also glosses it as no protector or retreat.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد، وقتادة، والسدي: لا ملجأ. وقال قتادة أيضا: {قل إني لن يجيرني من الله أحد ولن أجد من دونه ملتحدا} أي: لا نصير ولا ملجأ.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception for delivering God’s messages may qualify the Prophet’s lack of control over harm and guidance, or his inability to find refuge; only fulfilling the message assigned to him is his duty, as in another verse.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون استثناء من قوله: {لن يجيرني من الله أحد} أي: لا يجيرني منه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the food that chokes sticks in the throat and neither enters nor comes out.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ينشب في الحلق فلا يدخل ولا يخرج.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth and mountains will quake; mountains will become heaps of loose sand, then vanish until the ground is level, with no depression or rise.
rows.anchor: أي: تزلزل، {وكانت الجبال كثيبا مهيلا} أي: تصير ككثبان الرمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning addresses Quraysh and all people: their witnessing messenger resembles Moses sent to Pharaoh, who disobeyed and received severe punishment; denial of Muhammad deserves even worse destruction.
rows.anchor: ثم قال مخاطبا لكفار قريش، والمراد سائر الناس: {إنا أرسلنا إليكم رسولا شاهدا عليكم}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatada, al-Suddi, and al-Thawri explain the punishment of Pharaoh as severe.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وقتادة، والسدي، والثوري: {أخذا وبيلا} أي: شديدا،

rows.speaker: حكيم بن حزام
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet heard the sky groan, with an angel bowing or prostrating on every handspan; the excerpt gives no grading.
rows.anchor: عن حكيم بن حزام قال: بينما رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مع أصحابه

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: A strange Prophetic report from Aisha says no space in the lowest heaven is without an angel prostrating or standing and cites the angels’ declaration that each has a place.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة أنها قالت: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ما في السماء الدنيا موضع قدم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas‘ud gives a stopped report that every handspan of one heaven bears an angel’s forehead or feet in prayer, then recites the angels’ declaration.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود أنه قال: إن من السماوات سماء ما فيها موضع شبر إلا وعليه جبهة ملك

rows.speaker: العلاء بن سعد
rows.claim: A very strange-chain report says every foot-space in the heavens has a standing, bowing, or prostrating angel and quotes the angels’ declaration.
rows.anchor: عن أبيه العلاء بن سعد -وقد شهد الفتح وما بعده-أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال يوما لجلسائه:

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: In a report Ibn Kathir calls extremely objectionable, Umar relates an altercation over Abu Jahsh’s refusal to pray, then a saying that God has angels continuously bowing or prostrating who will say they never worshipped Him as He deserves.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمر: أن عمر جاء والصلاة قائمة، ونفر ثلاثة جلوس،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir calls this account highly objectionable and faults its transmission: Ishaq al-Farawi was weakened by several critics, his teacher was also criticized, and Muhammad ibn Nasr failed to discuss its defects.
rows.anchor: وهذا حديث غريب جدا، بل منكر نكارة شديدة، وإسحاق الفروي روى عنه البخاري،

rows.speaker: محمد بن نصر المروزي
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Nasr also transmits similar versions as mursal reports through Sa‘id ibn Jubayr and al-Hasan al-Basri.
rows.anchor: غير أنه رواه من وجه آخر عن سعيد بن جبير مرسلا بنحوه

rows.speaker: عدي بن أرطاة
rows.claim: A report with an acceptable chain says angels tremble in awe of God, some prostrating or bowing continuously since the creation of heaven and earth; when they raise their heads, they say they have not worshipped Him as He deserves.
rows.anchor: سمعت عدي بن أرطاة وهو يخطبنا على منبر المدائن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon loses its light.
rows.anchor: أي: ذهب ضوءه.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains the joining of sun and moon as their being rolled together; Ibn Zayd recites the verses about the sun being folded and stars scattered, while a reported reading from Ibn Mas‘ud adds “together.”
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: كورا. وقرأ ابن زيد عند تفسير هذه الآية: {إذا الشمس كورت وإذا النجوم انكدرت}

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas‘ud and other early authorities say that when people witness the horrors, they seek an escape but find no refuge; another verse likewise denies them a hiding place.
rows.anchor: قال ابن مسعود، وابن عباس، وسعيد بن جبير، وغير واحد من السلف: أي لا نجاة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All people return to God, their final destination.
rows.anchor: أي: المرجع والمصير.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each person is informed of every deed, old or recent and small or great, as another verse says all deeds will be present.
rows.anchor: أي: يخبر بجميع أعماله قديمها وحديثها، أولها وآخرها، صغيرها وكبيرها،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says a person’s hearing, sight, hands, feet, and other limbs testify against him.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {بل الإنسان على نفسه بصيرة} يقول: سمعه وبصره ويداه ورجلاه وجوارحه.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says a person is a witness against himself, yet can see others’ faults while overlooking his own; an old Gospel saying makes the same comparison of a speck and a beam.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: شاهد على نفسه. وفي رواية قال: إذا شئت -والله-رأيته بصيرا بعيوب الناس

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says that even if a person argues or makes excuses, he knows the truth about himself.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: {ولو ألقى معاذيره} ولو جادل عنها فهو بصير عليها.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says a false excuse will not be accepted at Judgment.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: {ولو ألقى معاذيره} ولو اعتذر يومئذ بباطل لا يقبل منه.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi, Ibn Zayd, al-Hasan, and others understand the phrase as the person’s argument or excuse; Ibn Jarir chooses this interpretation.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: {ولو ألقى معاذيره} حجته. وكذا قال ابن زيد، والحسن البصري، وغيرهم. واختاره ابن جرير.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The Meccan surah was among those the Prophet recited in Friday dawn prayer, together with al-Sajda, according to a report in Sahih Muslim.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقرأ في صلاة الصبح يوم الجمعة

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd gives a strange mursal report that a Black man died after hearing the surah’s description of Paradise; the Prophet said longing for Paradise had taken his life.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن وهب: أخبرنا ابن زيد: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ هذه السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God bestowed the Qur’an, the Prophet should patiently accept His decree, refuse sinful or disbelieving people if they try to turn him from revelation, convey it, and trust God’s protection; “sinner” concerns deeds and “ungrateful disbeliever” the heart.
rows.anchor: أي: كما أكرمتك بما أنزلت عليك، فاصبر على قضائه وقدره، واعلم أنه سيدبرك بحسن تدبيره،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering God morning and evening means at the beginning and end of the day.
rows.anchor: أي: أول النهار وآخره.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night prayer and glorification are also commanded, as in the instructions for night vigil in al-Isra and al-Muzzammil.
rows.anchor: كقوله: {ومن الليل فتهجد به نافلة لك عسى أن يبعثك ربك مقاما محمودا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers prefer immediate worldly life and leave behind the weighty Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: منكرا على الكفار ومن أشبههم في حب الدنيا والإقبال عليها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and others take “strengthened their constitution” to mean that God created them.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وغير واحد: يعني خلقهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement about replacing people most likely means resurrecting and recreating them; initial creation proves resurrection is possible.
rows.anchor: أي: وإذا شئنا بعثناهم يوم القيامة، وبدلناهم فأعدناهم خلقا جديدا.

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd and Ibn Jarir instead understand replacement as God bringing another people in their place, as in other verses.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد، وابن جرير: {وإذا شئنا بدلنا أمثالهم تبديلا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is a reminder, and whoever wills may take a path to God by accepting the Qur’an’s guidance, as another verse urges belief and spending.
rows.anchor: ثم قال تعالى: {إن هذه} يعني: هذه السورة {تذكرة فمن شاء اتخذ إلى ربه سبيلا}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Awfi reports Ibn Abbas interpreting “the rain-bearing” as the wind; Ibn Abi Hatim also transmits this from Ibn Abbas through Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, and several early authorities agree that winds draw rain from clouds.
rows.anchor: قال العوفي، عن ابن عباس: {المعصرات} الريح.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas also says the phrase means clouds; Ikrima, Abu al-Aliya, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan, al-Rabi‘, and al-Thawri agree, and Ibn Jarir prefers this view.
rows.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: {من المعصرات} أي: من السحاب.

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra’ defines them as clouds ready to release rain but not yet raining, comparing the word to a woman nearing menstruation.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: هي السحاب التي تتحلب بالمطر ولم تمطر بعد،

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada reportedly interpret the phrase as the heavens; Ibn Kathir calls this an unusual view.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن، وقتادة: {من المعصرات} يعني: السموات. وهذا قول غريب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clearest interpretation is clouds, supported by the verse saying rain emerges from within clouds.
rows.anchor: والأظهر أن المراد بالمعصرات: السحاب،

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid, Qatada, and al-Rabi‘ say “pouring” means water cascading down; al-Thawri says continuous and Ibn Zayd says abundant.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد، وقتادة، والربيع بن أنس: {ثجاجا} منصبا. وقال الثوري: متتابعا.

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir says thajj is not used in Arabic to mean mere abundance but means consecutive pouring; he cites the Prophetic phrase “the best pilgrimage is calling aloud and pouring,” referring to sacrificial blood.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جرير: ولا يعرف في كلام العرب في صفة الكثرة الثج، وإنما الثج: الصب المتتابع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report about a woman with prolonged bleeding using thajj supports its sense of repeated, abundant flow.
rows.anchor: وهذا فيه دلالة على استعمال الثج في الصب المتتابع الكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God uses abundant, beneficial rain to grow grain stored for people and livestock, edible fresh plants, and gardens with varied fruits, colors, flavors, and scents.
rows.anchor: أي: لنخرج بهذا الماء الكثير الطيب النافع المبارك {حبا} يدخر للأناسي والأنعام،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and others explain “interwoven gardens” as gardens growing together, comparing their diversity despite shared water to another verse.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس، وغيره: {ألفافا} مجتمعة.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The Great Overwhelming is Resurrection; it is so named because it overwhelms every dreadful matter, as another verse says the Hour is more grievous.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن عباس، سميت بذلك لأنها تطم على كل أمر هائل مفظع،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At that time every person recalls all of his good and bad deeds, as another verse says.
rows.anchor: حينئذ يتذكر ابن آدم جميع عمله خيره وشره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell will be exposed so people see it directly.
rows.anchor: أي: أظهرت للناظرين فرآها الناس عيانا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebel is one who defies God and prefers worldly life over religion and the Hereafter; Hell is his destination, with food from zaqqum and drink of boiling water.
rows.anchor: أي: تمرد وعتا، {وآثر الحياة الدنيا} أي: قدمها على أمر دينه وأخراه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fearing one’s Lord means fearing to stand before Him and face His judgment, and restraining desire by returning oneself to obedience.
rows.anchor: أي: خاف القيام بين يدي الله عز وجل، وخاف حكم الله فيه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person who restrains desire will return to Paradise as his final abode.
rows.anchor: أي: منقلبه ومصيره ومرجعه إلى الجنة الفيحاء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God knows the appointed time of the Hour; its knowledge is beyond the Prophet and all creation, as another verse says.
rows.anchor: أي: ليس علمها إليك ولا إلى أحد من الخلق، بل مردها ومرجعها إلى الله عز وجل،

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: When Gabriel asked the Prophet when the Hour would come, he replied that the one asked knew no more than the asker.
rows.anchor: جبريل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن وقت الساعة قال: "ما المسئول عنها بأعلم من السائل".

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet was sent to warn people of God’s might and punishment; whoever fears God and His warning follows him and succeeds, while rejecters fail.
rows.anchor: إنما بعثتك لتنذر الناس وتحذرهم من بأس الله وعذابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When raised from their graves, people will consider worldly life so brief it seemed like part of one afternoon or morning.
rows.anchor: إذا قاموا من قبورهم إلى المحشر يستقصرون مدة الحياة الدنيا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas defines evening as noon to sunset and morning as sunrise to noon.
rows.anchor: قال جويبر، عن الضحاك، عن ابن عباس: {كأنهم يوم يرونها لم يلبثوا إلا عشية أو ضحاها} أما عشية: فما بين الظهر إلى غروب الشمس،

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the whole duration of worldly life will seem brief when people behold the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: وقت الدنيا في أعين القوم حين عاينوا الآخرة.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Deafening Blast is a name for Resurrection, magnified by God as a warning; Ibn Jarir suggests it may name the trumpet blast itself.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (الصاخة) اسم من أسماء يوم القيامة، عظمه الله، وحذره عباده.

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawi says the term means the cry of Resurrection because it strikes the ears so forcefully it nearly deafens them.
rows.anchor: وقال البغوي: (الصاخة) يعني صيحة القيامة؛ سميت بذلك لأنها تصخ الأسماع،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People will see their relatives yet flee from them because the terror and ordeal are so great.
rows.anchor: أي: يراهم، ويفر منهم، ويبتعد عنهم؛ لأن الهول عظيم، والخطب جليل.

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima describes spouses and children refusing even one good deed requested by a relative at Judgment, fearing they need their own deeds to escape.
rows.anchor: قال عكرمة: يلقى الرجل زوجته فيقول لها: يا هذه، أي بعل كنت لك؟

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: In the authentic intercession report, the resolute messengers each say “myself”; even Jesus asks only for himself, not Mary, his mother.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث الصحيح-في أمر الشفاعة-: أنه إذا طلب إلى كل من أولي العزم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says people flee from those they love most and from their closest relatives because of the terror of that Day.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: الأحب فالأحب، والأقرب فالأقرب، من هول ذلك اليوم.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, as transmitted by Ibn Abi Talha, identifies the hidden, moving bodies as wild cattle; Ibn Abbas elsewhere and several early authorities identify them as gazelles, while Abu al-Sha‘tha includes both.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس: {الجواري الكنس} قال:

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says people had reported that the verses mean stars, but what they themselves heard was that they mean wild cattle sheltering in their lairs.
rows.anchor: فقال مجاهد: كنا نسمع فيها شيئا، وناس يقولون: إنها النجوم.

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir does not decide between stars, gazelles, and wild cattle; he says all may be intended.
rows.anchor: وتوقف ابن جرير في قوله: {الخنس الجواري الكنس} هل هو النجوم، أو الظباء وبقر الوحش؟
